mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicate accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Core CPI inflation exceeding 275.0 (1982-1984=100) signals accelerating price pressures, triggering central bank tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >45% of triggered periods (CPIAUCSL > 275.0), or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions with unemployment below 4.0% and declining, labor market tightness supports corporate profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >45% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and falling, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained industrial production growth above 100.5 (2017=100) signals robust manufacturing activity, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when INDPRO > 100.5, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth exceeding 2.0% annualized indicates strong economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >45% of triggered periods (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized), or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS rising) and unemployment decline (UNRATE falling) signal labor market tightening, preceding corporate wage pressures and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict positive returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and rising for 3 months) increase discount rates and reduce risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >45% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and rising for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.02.
